title: pub Visibility
concept: The `pub` keyword marks items as part of a module's public API
why: Encapsulation is meaningless if you cannot selectively expose an API. `pub` defines the contract between a module and its consumers. It lets library authors evolve internal details without breaking downstream code, while clearly signaling which functions, types, and constants are stable and supported.
theory: XIOM's visibility model has three levels: **private** (default, accessible only within the declaring module), **pub** (accessible from parent modules and external crates), and **pub(crate)** (accessible anywhere within the same crate but not externally). The `pub` modifier can be placed on `fn`, `struct`, `enum`, `const`, `var`, and `type` declarations. A `pub` struct with private fields still has controlled access — users can construct it but not read internals directly.
tips: Start with everything private; add `pub` only when needed
Group `pub` items together at the top of a module
`pub(crate)` is ideal for shared internal utilities across a crate
common_mistakes: Marking everything `pub` by habit — defeats encapsulation
Forgetting `pub` on enum variants when exposing an enum
Assuming `pub` on a struct auto-publishes its fields
